images.title: Two walks in fortieths
images.purpose: Show that 3/4 km is longer than 7/10 km: written in fortieths, 30/40 is more than 28/40.
images.composition: Two long road strips stacked with wide space between them, left edges aligned, and one comparison line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Top: one long strip for 1 km cut into 4 equal parts, the first 3 parts filled teal #0072B2. Below: one strip of exactly the same length, left edges aligned, cut into 10 equal parts, the first 7 parts filled amber #E69F00. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket marks the small extra length where the teal fill goes past the amber fill. Centred below: one comparison line. Exactly 2 strips, 3 teal parts, 7 amber parts, 1 bracket.

images.takeaway: Step 1: make the denominators the same. Step 2: compare the numerators.
images.description: Two aligned 1 km strips: 3 of 4 parts teal and 7 of 10 parts amber; a bracket shows the teal reaches further, and the line 30/40 > 28/40 compares them in the same unit.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two outlined parts and say how much farther Joseph walks in fortieths of a kilometre.

image_decisions.why: Strips recut into the same parts show the two steps of comparing in one picture.
